note: Economy difficulty. These multipliers change the PLAYER's operating position only; NPC carriers, prices and the rest of the world run on the base economy at every level, so a harder level means a harder life for you, not a different universe. target_margin is the net margin the benchmark ship (the starter) should earn on the reference lane mix; tests/test_economy_levels.gd checks each level lands inside its band, and tools like it retune the multipliers when the economy changes. Multipliers were solved with tests/solve_levels.gd (bisect freight_pay_mult against target margin); rerun it whenever base rates, fuel, ship costs or the starter ship change. freight_pay_mult above 1 is the owner-operator premium (small, odd and urgent loads pay more per SCU than trunk freight); the consignee pays it, so money is conserved.

benchmark.note: The benchmark captain is the starter ship worked by a stand-in (tests/test_player_economy.gd): paid time 98% (the known-space world always has more freight than one small ship can carry), 70% of return legs also loaded, and realised rates 1.32x the list rate (urgency premiums on goods in short supply, and escalated rates on freight nobody has picked up). The stand-ins see freight before the NPC fleets, as the human does (carrier flag first_look). rate_premium is fitted by tests/solve_levels_sim.gd so the quick probe agrees with the full simulation at the normal level. A captain who is idle more, or who flies empty, loses money. The benchmark ship is ShipPresets.STARTER_FTL: the plain starter with an FTL drive and the radiator it needs fitted (interstellar freight needs a drive; the plain starter is sublight and works local runs, see local_pay_mult).

difficulty_ids_match: Level ids match Worlds.DIFFICULTIES ids, so the difficulty chosen at New Game selects the economy level.
local_note: local_pay_mult scales in-system (sublight) job pay. Solved with tests/solve_local.gd: a stand-in captain with the plain starter takes the best-paying run available for 120 days; the net per day after fuel, berth fees, wages and ownership is bisected to local_target_net_per_day. The tank, not the board, is the limit on long hops, so net income is steep in this multiplier: re-solve whenever fuel, crew costs, the starter or local_space.json change.
